caption: The drawing depicts a painted statue of a standing male figure positioned on a rectangular base. The figure is dressed in a short, green tunic with yellow decorative patterns and a red sash draped across the torso and tied at the waist. He is wearing a short, red-brown helmet or cap with an upturned front and a green band wrapping around it, and his long, dark hair flows below the helmet, over his shoulders. The man stands with his left leg slightly forward and his left arm extending outward, holding a rectangular object that appears to be a bundle or a book. His right arm hangs by his side, and his feet are bare. He has some wrapped bands around his forearms and lower legs, similar in color to his sash. The statue is balanced by a vertical support structure attached behind the figure from the base up to his mid-back. The background of the drawing is plain and off-white, and the artist’s signature “R. Chiardi” is visible near the bottom right of the image.
title: Cigar Store Indian
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
